answer: Sand-bar grazing rights wait on a filmed tracer recapture. A claimant posts 36 coins and drops a clerk-stamped 48-gram granite chip, tagged sparrow, at stake 4 of licensed riffle B, whose chainage is printed on atlas sheet 12 of the published reach. After six hours of gauged flow the same chip must be lifted at least 80 metres downstream, with GPS stills and the river staff reading hashed onto the lot ticket. Peers recompute travel against the sheet chainage. A reused chip or a dry-planted pickup burns the bond and voids the batch.
